title: Ordinary coefficient categories underlying finite discrete realization
statement: Let B be a commutative topological ring and T a scheme. Let B_T be the pulled-back condensed continuous-function ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Define FiniteDiscreteInternalModules B T as internal B_T-modules in abelian pro-etale sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Define FiniteDiscreteProEtaleSheaves B T as sheaves on T_proet with values in modules over ULift B, and FiniteDiscreteEtalePlus B T as the bounded-below ordinary derived category of module-valued sheaves on T_et [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Every equivalence E from the pro-etale module-valued category to the internal module category has additive underlying functor, because an equivalence between these preadditive categories preserves binary products. These are exactly the existing category abbreviations and instance used by finite-discrete realization; the definitions do not impose bounded constructibility or any noetherian condition.

source.place: Section 5.1, ordinary module-valued coefficient categories; existing FiniteDiscreteRealizationFunctor category abbreviations

proof.text: Use the existing internal module category for B_T, the ordinary module-valued sheaf category for T_proet, and the Plus subcategory of the ordinary etale derived category. This is just the relocation of the three existing category abbreviations, with identical signatures and bodies, from FiniteDiscreteRealizationFunctor. The unchanged additive instance follows from the existing Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products theorem.
